title: What's Actually Live?

narrative.intro: Customers are reporting the app is slow. The team's internal status page says "v1.4.2 - deployed and healthy" - the perf-improvements release everyone's been excited about. But the status page hasn't been touched in weeks, and the on-call channel says there was some kind of rollback last month. You pull up prod's actual ref to find out what's really running.
narrative.correctDebrief: Correct - prod isn't on v1.4.2 at all. It's on an untagged revert commit built on top of v1.4.1, from a rollback nobody ever recorded anywhere official. The status page kept claiming v1.4.2 because updating it was never part of the rollback - the actual deployed state and the claimed state just quietly drifted apart. That's the whole failure mode Status Accounting exists to prevent: a claim about "what's in prod" is worthless unless something's actually keeping it in sync with prod's real ref.
narrative.incorrectDebrief: Don't trust the status page - follow prod's ref directly, back through its own parent chain. It doesn't land on v1.4.2's tag, and it doesn't land on v1.4.1's tag either. It's a commit with no release tag on it at all.

c2.message: release: cut v1.4.1 - hotfix for auth bug

c4.message: revert: roll back v1.4.2 - perf change caused a memory leak

prompt: The status page says v1.4.2 is live. What does prod's ref actually point to?

options.label: v1.4.2, exactly what the status page claims
A rollback commit with no release tag at all
